result.summary: All eight round-1 findings are resolved. The two MAJORs are fixed: every new public function now has a full @spec with argument names, element types and error shape (section 8.2 and the design's spec blocks for RequiredOutputs, SemanticValidation additions, SeparationOfDuties.check/5 and check_for_claim/3, the private blocking_nodes/5, completion_guards_result/0), and step 4b, section 8.2 and the REQ-463 adjustment now all name exactly one engine entry point, SeparationOfDuties.check/5. Section 2 was re-derived again from engine.ex run_complete_task (2263-2365) and still matches step for step, now including the function-level rescue as exit path 8z. No regression: twelve sections present, traceability A1-A11/C1-C7 intact, section 3/4 literal bodies intact (rule A body exactly {"detail":"separation of duties","status":403}), code fences hold only JSON and @spec/@type, no TBD/deferral language. One cosmetic advisory remains (check_for_claim actor_id type is narrower in section 6 than in 8.2); it does not block.

findings.text: Verified fixed. Section 8.2 now specs RequiredOutputs.required_outputs/1 (Node.t() -> [String.t()]), missing_keys/2 (required :: [String.t()], output_variables :: map() -> sorted [String.t()]), rejected_keys/2 (validations :: VariableMerge.variable_validations(), exclude :: [String.t()] -> sorted [String.t()]); SemanticValidation.required_output_schema_violations/2 (graph, declared_fields) -> [Violation.t()] and decision_key_warnings/2 (graph, definition_name) -> [String.t()] with the reason the definition name is the second argument; SeparationOfDuties.check/5 (repo, graph, task, actor_id, prefix) -> :ok | {:error, {:separation_of_duties, [String.t()]}}; check_for_claim/3; private blocking_nodes/5; and completion_guards_result/0 = {:ok, :guards_passed | :no_guards} | {:error, {:completion_refused, completion_refusal()}}. Step 4a also states the pass payload. Referenced types exist in lib: VariableMerge.variable_validations (variable_merge.ex:170), SemanticValidation.declared_fields (semantic_validation.ex:169), Engine.Task.t (task.ex:79), Graph.t and Node.t (graph.ex).

Verified fixed. Step 4b (section 2.2), section 8.2 header comment and the REQ-463 adjustment item 1 all say the engine step calls SeparationOfDuties.check/5 only; blocking_nodes/5 is private and not called by the engine; check_for_claim/3 is the claim path entry and delegates to check/5. grep of SeparationOfDuties/blocking_nodes in the design shows no remaining second entry point.
Step 4a now limits the byte-identical claim to step 4 and states that step 6b-iv refuses a schema-rejected value on every HUMAN_TASK completion, which is why the five existing tests change.
Section 1.4 reason 1 now says SemanticValidation runs at validate_definition_graph and activate and does NOT run in create/2 (definitions.ex:557-561). Correct.

Citations section now reads lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex (1347-1352, core_role_allows?(:TENANT_ADMIN) at 1352, grep-confirmed at line 1352), assign_task def 608, reassign_task def 678 (grep-confirmed), merge def 210 (spec 205), reevaluate def 161 (spec 154), scheduler escalation arm at 312 (grep-confirmed).

New item 8z documents the function-level rescue (engine.ex:2362-2364) as an exit path covering every step including new step 4 and 6b, yielding {:error, {:transaction_failed, exception}}, router 500 (routers/tasks.ex:425, grep-confirmed generic {:error, _reason} clause), no refusal audit row, no refusal body. Matches the code: the rescue wraps the whole pipeline through interpret_complete_result.

Design adds REQ-462 item 0 and item 2 saying ORCH must reword REQ-462 BUILDS item 3 and acceptance line 4 before dispatch, and REQ-461 item 4 states the actual surfaces (check 3 and 4 warnings at validate and pack install only). ORCH action still required: amend REQ-462 text before dispatching it.

Section 2.4 now states the guarantee as at most one audit record per refused request, exactly one when the audit store is healthy (D-3). Section 2.2 step 4 now decides the computed-field question explicitly: authors must not list computed fields in required_outputs, step 4c judges the submitted map, no validator check added. REVIEWER should still confirm D-3 and this decision.

Section 6 spec for check_for_claim/3 types actor_id as String.t(), while section 8.2 types it Ecto.UUID.t() | String.t() | nil and says check/5 returns :ok for a non-binary actor. The two should read the same; ELIXIR-DEV should use the 8.2 union (the more permissive one). Does not change behaviour or ambiguity of any step.
